I built KVFabric — a distributed KV cache fabric that eliminates redundant prefill computation in LLM inference by sharing KV caches across GPU nodes over the network.

The core insight: when multiple inference nodes serve overlapping prompts (system prompts, few-shot examples, shared context), each node redundantly recomputes the same KV cache. KVFabric intercepts this at the attention layer, registers computed caches in a prefix trie with cumulative xxhash3-128 hashing, and routes incoming requests to nodes that already hold matching prefixes — turning expensive GPU prefill into a fast TCP transfer.

The system is a Rust workspace (wire protocol, prefix trie, TCP transfer, HTTP routing proxy with Prometheus metrics) plus a Python adapter that integrates natively with vLLM's KV Connector API. I verified it end-to-end on real GPUs: two-node cache sharing on T4s showed 73-76% prefill savings, and the connector runs inside vLLM's V1 engine on A10Gs, surviving subprocess spawns and handling the full load/save lifecycle across scheduler and worker roles.

I wrote 140 tests across Rust unit tests, Python CPU tests, and GPU integration tests (run remotely via Modal on T4/A10G hardware). The whole thing is designed to fail gracefully — every failure path falls back to normal recompute, so it never crashes inference.

## What is KVFabric?

KVFabric is a distributed KV cache fabric for LLM inference. It eliminates redundant prefill computation by sharing KV caches across GPU inference nodes over the network. When multiple inference nodes serve overlapping prompts (system prompts, few-shot examples, shared context), each node normally recomputes the same KV cache from scratch. KVFabric intercepts this at the attention layer, registers computed caches in a prefix trie, and routes incoming requests to nodes that already hold matching prefixes — turning expensive GPU prefill into a fast TCP transfer.

**Core principle**: "Every failure path ends in recompute. Never worse than not having the product."

**Result**: 73-76% prefill savings verified on real GPUs in two-node cache sharing.

**Describe your company or idea in a single sentence:**

KVFabric is a distributed KV cache fabric that eliminates redundant prefill computation in multi-node LLM inference by sharing KV caches across GPUs over the network, cutting prefill costs by 73-76%.

---

**Why are you working on this idea?**

Every major LLM deployment wastes GPU compute recomputing the same KV caches. When you have 8 inference nodes and they all serve requests with the same system prompt, each node independently computes identical KV caches from scratch — that's 7x wasted prefill. Existing prefix caching only works within a single node. Nobody has solved the cross-node problem cleanly. I built the full system — Rust core for the router, wire protocol, and prefix trie, plus a Python adapter that plugs directly into vLLM's native KV Connector API — and proved it works on real GPUs with 73-76% prefill savings. As inference deployments scale and prompts get longer (agents, RAG, tool use), this waste compounds. I want to make it the default infrastructure layer for multi-node LLM serving.

---

**How far along are you? Describe your progress to-date:**

Fully built and GPU-verified. The system has 5 Rust crates (wire protocol, prefix trie with xxhash3 hashing, TCP transfer, HTTP routing proxy with Prometheus metrics) and a Python vLLM adapter that integrates natively with vLLM's V1 KV Connector API. I've written 140 tests — 41 Rust, 78 Python CPU, and 21 GPU integration tests running on real T4 and A10G hardware via Modal. Two-node cache sharing is byte-perfect with measured 73-76% prefill savings. The connector runs inside vLLM's V1 engine, surviving multiprocessing subprocess spawns across scheduler and worker processes. Every failure path falls back to normal recompute — the system is never worse than not having it. Next steps are distributed trie for >200 node scale and CacheGen-style compression for transfer bandwidth reduction.
